item.title: [Featured Article] Grace Coolidge
item.description: Grace Anna Coolidge was first lady of the United States from 1923 to 1929 as the wife of the 30th president of the United States, Calvin Coolidge. She was previously the second lady of the United States from 1921 to 1923 and the first lady of Massachusetts from 1919 to 1921.

item.title: [In the News] A ferry fire off Coron, Palawan, Philippines, kills at least 76 people.
item.description: On the evening of September 9, 2026, the Philippine passenger-cargo vessel MV June Aster caught fire in the waters off Coron, Palawan. The ferry was carrying 115 passengers and 17 crew members when the fire broke out. The fire was reported at around 6:45 p.m. PHT (UTC+8) approximately 1.2 nautical miles northeast of Barangay Marcilla in Coron. At least 76 people on board were killed, while 43 were rescued and 13 remain missing.

item.title: [In the News] In Yemen, heavy fighting between the Houthis and the Presidential Leadership Council leaves hundreds of people dead.
item.description: On 3 September 2026, heavy fighting broke out between the Houthis and the Government of Yemen amid the ongoing Yemeni civil war. Clashes began with a Houthi offensive in Taiz Governorate, prompting a PLC counter-offensive against Houthis in the Al-Jawf and Al-Bayda governorates.

item.title: [In the News] American journalist and feminist activist Gloria Steinem dies at the age of 92.
item.description: Gloria Marie Steinem was an American journalist and social movement activist who emerged as a nationally recognized leader of second-wave feminism in the United States in the late 1960s and early 1970s, and who remained particularly prominent in the 1980s and early 1990s.

item.title: [In the News] Duane Davis is convicted of orchestrating the 1996 murder of American rapper Tupac Shakur.
item.description: On September 7, 1996, at 11:15 p.m. (PDT), Tupac Shakur, a 25-year-old American rapper, was shot in a drive-by shooting in Paradise, Nevada. The shooting occurred when the car carrying Shakur was stopped at a red light at East Flamingo Road and Koval Lane. Shakur was struck by four rounds fired from a .40-caliber Glock 22 pistol — two in the chest, one in the arm and one in the thigh. The driver, Death Row Records executive Suge Knight, was struck in the head by bullet fragments. Shakur died from his injuries six days later.
